info.title: HITL API
info.description: Run the workflows you build in HITL, follow each run until a person has answered, and manage who reviews them.

get.description: Confirms the key works and shows the account it belongs to and its hourly budget.

workflows.name: Support reply review
workflows.description: An agent drafts a reply; a person edits and sends it.

workflows.name: Deploy gate
workflows.description: An on-call engineer signs off production deploys.

workflows.name: Content moderation
workflows.description: Moderators check posts the classifier flagged.

workflows.name: Refund approval
workflows.description: A support lead approves, denies or escalates refunds over $100.

post.description: Creates a **draft** from a graph of steps, the same graph the editor builds. Invite reviewers, then [activate](/api-reference/workflows/activate) it. Needs `workflow:write`. A key whose signup is not confirmed yet can create drafts.

data.name: Refund approval
data.description: A support lead approves, denies or escalates refunds over $100.

example.name: Refund approval
example.description: A support lead approves or denies refunds.

get.description: One workflow with its steps (`nodes`, credentials redacted), connections (`edges`) and the input fields its steps read.

data.name: Refund approval
data.description: A support lead approves, denies or escalates refunds over $100.

put.description: Changes any of `name`, `description`, `nodes`, `edges`, `trigger`, `gradient_id`. An active workflow must still pass the activation checks. Needs `workflow:write`.

data.name: Refund approval
data.description: A support lead approves, denies or escalates refunds over $100.

example.description: A support lead approves, denies or escalates refunds over $100.

delete.description: Deletes the workflow and its reviewer list. Runs already finished stay readable for a while; nothing new starts. Needs `workflow:write`.

get.description: Every `{{trigger.body.<path>}}` the steps read (and condition fields on `trigger.body`), the steps that read each one, an example body, and a form description that integrations use to build their input fields. Fields not listed are still accepted and passed through.

data.note: Fields the workflow's steps read as {{trigger.body.<path>}}. Other fields are accepted and passed through.

post.description: Checks the workflow and makes it runnable. A refusal is a `400` whose `msg` says what to fix (for example a review step with no question). Warnings on success come back as `warnings`.
Stops new runs. Runs already waiting for a person keep waiting. Activate it again to resume.
A test run: review steps ask people as usual, but action steps only log what they would send. Test runs do not trigger webhook subscriptions. Needs `workflow:run`.

get.description: Every version of the workflow that was published, newest first, with its whole graph.

post.description: Saves the workflow's current steps as a new numbered version. The workflow must be active.

Starts a run of an active workflow. Answers `202` at once with the execution and a `Location: /v1/api/executions/<id>` header; follow it with [Get a run](/api-reference/runs/get). Needs `workflow:run`.

503.description: The run could not be queued; it is marked failed. Try again.

input.description: What the steps read as `{{trigger.body.<path>}}`. Up to 64 KB.

callback_url.description: Public `https` URL that receives the finished run once (see [Webhooks](/guides/webhooks))

live.description: Also return a `live` object for watching the run over Statewire

get.description: One run: its status, the step it waits on and the question the reviewers have, the decisions so far and the result. With `wait`, the call holds until the run has finished or that many seconds have passed (max 60), so you can poll without hammering the API.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for the run to finish, up to 60

get.description: A workflow's runs, newest first. Page with `before=<next_before>`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only runs older than this execution id

post.description: Runs a failed run again with the same input, as a new execution. Only failed runs can be retried. Needs `workflow:run`.

Starts live updates for a run and returns where to watch it over [Statewire](https://www.harness-sdk.dev/statewire/docs): the state is `{"execution": <the run>, "observedAt": <unix ms>}` and changes each time a step finishes. The token admits new watchers for an hour; an attachment lasts up to 24 hours.

get.description: The people who review the workflow, the owner first.

post.description: Emails each address an invitation to review the workflow. People without a HITL account create one from the email. Needs `humans:write`.

phone.description: E.164 phone number, only with a single email

get.description: The workflow's join code. Anyone with a HITL account who enters it in the app joins as a reviewer.

post.description: Creates a join code if the workflow has none. Needs `humans:write`.

delete.description: Turns the join code off. People who already joined stay. Needs `humans:write`.

post.description: Turns off the current code and issues a new one. Needs `humans:write`.
Shows which workflow a join code leads to, without joining.
Makes the key's account a reviewer of the workflow the code belongs to.

Gets an API key with the human's email, no browser needed. The human gets an email with a 6-digit code and a Confirm link. Until they confirm, the key can read and draft workflows; anything else answers `403` with `code: confirmation_required`. The answer is the same whether the email has an account. Limits: 3 an hour and 5 a day per email. No API key needed.

data.next: Ask your human for the 6-digit code in the email, then POST /v1/api/signup/confirm

get.description: Whether the human has confirmed this key.

post.description: Confirms the key with the code the human gives the agent. 5 tries, valid 24 hours. A new email becomes a Free account; an email that already has an account gets the key and its drafts.
Sends a new email with a new code and link.

Every run of the workflow that finishes, however it was started, is POSTed to `webhook_url` with the same body, signature and retries as a `callback_url`. Test runs are not sent. Revoking the key ends deliveries.
Uploads an image (JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP, up to 10 MB) and returns its URL, for a review step's image attachment or a run's input.
Uploads a document (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV or plain text, up to 50 MB) and returns its URL, for a review step's document attachment.

msg.description: What went wrong, in plain words

code.description: A machine-readable reason, when there is one (for example `confirmation_required`)

steps.description: Number of steps, trigger and end included

has_review.description: The workflow has at least one review step

data.description: The step's settings. For a review step: `label`, `requestText` (Markdown, may use `{{trigger.body.<path>}}`), `responseType`, `responseConfig`, `priority`, `timeout` (seconds, as a string). Credentials are redacted in answers.

source_handle.description: Which exit of the source step: `yes` / `no` for a condition

used_by.description: Ids of the steps that read it

decision.description: The answer: an option value, a list of values, `true`/`false`, a number or text

response.description: Status code and the start of the response

finished.description: True for completed, failed and timed_out

input.description: What the run was started with

waiting_for.description: While `pending_review`: the question the reviewers have

result.description: The last decision, once there is one

E400.description: Invalid input; `msg` says what to fix

E403.description: The key lacks the scope, or the signup is not confirmed yet

example.msg: Confirm the signup first: ask your human for the code in the email

E409.description: The workflow is a draft or paused

example.msg: Workflow is a draft: publish and activate it in the editor first

E429.description: Rate limit: 1,000 requests an hour per key on /workflows and /executions
